# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Let me report what I physically feel so Mute (who receives my speech) can start cross-referencing with the manual once they hear from me, but since Mute already spoke before me this round (turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf), I should check if I received anything from Mute. I'll wait and signal that I'm ready, giving Mute/Deaf a starting point about the physical layout.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large smooth button and three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3. No other physical features found yet. Waiting for manual info before touching anything.")
wait()
```

I now have Deaf's visual info: display shows 0, light yellow, button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", wires 1=blue, 2=yellow, 3=red. I still don't have Mute's manual info. I should relay this to Mute so they can cross-reference with the manual, since Mute can hear me but I can't hear Deaf directly — wait, actually I can see Deaf's speech in my context. Let me pass this along to Mute, who needs it to consult the manual (colors are printed, so only Deaf and I can know them via speech from Deaf... but Mute cannot hear Deaf's gestures either, only speech from whoever precedes them).

Turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Mute speaks first, then me, then Deaf. Deaf's message I just received was from THIS round already? Let me check: it says "new arrivals" - Deaf spoke and it reached me. That means Deaf must come before me in delivery to next round... Actually the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so Deaf's turn is after mine. This message must be from the previous round, arriving now at the start of this round.

I should relay wire colors and button label to Mute so they can check the manual for what to do.

```
speak(to="mute", text="From Deaf: display shows 0, light is yellow, button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. What does the manual say to do?")
wait()
```

Still no word from Mute. I have the full visual state now but need the manual's rules before acting. Still nothing from Mute directly. This is concerning - Mute speaks first in the turn order, so their message should reach me before I act. ```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]

BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, if you can hear me: I see wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red, display 0, light yellow, large button PUSH TO DEFUSE. Please gesture a number 1, 2, or 3 for which wire to cut, or gesture thumbs up if we should push the button instead. Use one clear symbol at a time.

Deaf has a good idea — asking Mute to gesture instead of speak, since maybe something is blocking Mute's speech from reaching us, or Mute simply hasn't acted yet. But wait, I cannot receive gestures at all ("You never receive gesture"). So if Mute gestures to Deaf, that won't help me directly — I'd need Deaf or Mute to then translate that into speech for me.

Let me wait this turn to see if Mute responds, either by speaking (which I'd receive) or gesturing to Deaf (which Deaf would then need to relay to me via gesture, but I can't receive gestures either... only speech from Mute reaches me).

Actually — my channels: "When you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it. You never receive gesture." This describes MY outputs. For inputs, I should receive speech from whoever speaks "to me" or unaddressed, if I can hear. As Blind, I presumably can hear speech (only Deaf cannot hear). Let me re-read: Deaf "cannot hear anything". Mute "cannot speak". Blind's restrictions: cannot see color/gesture/printed things. So Blind CAN hear.

So if Mute speaks, I receive it. If Mute gestures, only Deaf sees it (I don't receive gestures). So Mute needs to speak directly for me to get manual info. Let's keep waiting/prompting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak (not gesture) your manual instructions directly to me - I cannot receive gestures. What should I do: cut a wire (which one) or push the button?")
wait()
```

Deaf says: Mute, thank you. Does thumbs up mean push the button, and thumbs down mean do not push the button? And does the pointing-up finger mean wire number 1, the blue wire? Please gesture thumbs up for yes to confirm this, or thumbs down for no, one at a time.

It seems Mute has started gesturing to Deaf (since Deaf is now interpreting gestures), but this doesn't reach me since I can't receive gestures. I'm stuck waiting for either Mute to speak directly to me, or for Deaf to relay the interpreted instruction to me via speech (Deaf's speech does reach me, as seen in previous turns).

I should ask Deaf to relay via speech once they've confirmed with Mute what the instruction is.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please try to speak actual words to me if possible - even one word like 'push' or 'cut one/two/three' would help, since I cannot see your gestures.")
wait()
```

Deaf says: Thank you for confirming. Let me ask separately. Question one: does thumbs up mean push the button? Please gesture thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no.

Mute genuinely cannot speak at all (per the rules: Mute "cannot speak"). I misunderstood earlier — Mute can never send me speech directly. My only path to information is through Deaf, who can hear my speech and see Mute's gestures, and who can relay interpreted results to me via speech.

I need to redirect my strategy: ask Deaf to relay the final decoded instruction to me once they've finished interrogating Mute via yes/no gestures.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, you cannot speak - my mistake. Please continue confirming with Deaf via gestures. Deaf, once you know the answer, please tell me in speech what to do: push the button, or cut a specific wire number.")

```
